newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen dives on panic selling after tankan.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen dives on panic selling after tankan.

text.p: The key March three-month Euroyen futures contract dived by midday on Wednesday due to panic selling after better-than-expected results for the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) quarterly "tankan" corporate sentiment survey.
"The tankan pulled the rug out from under the Euroyen," said a European bank trader. The March tumbled to a low of 98.73 from 98.94 on Tuesday. It stood at 98.75 at around noon.

The tankan showed that big Japanese manufacturers grew much more optimistic this month, marking a clear contrast with the market's expectation that their sentiment may have turned sour along with non-manufacturers and smaller firms.

The tankan showed that the major manufacturers' diffusion index (DI) -- the percentage difference between corporate managers seeing business conditions favourable and those feeling that conditions are unfavourable -- was plus seven, against plus two in the preceding survey in March. Their September DI forecast was plus eight. The majority of the market had expected the DI to fall into negative territory.

Masayuki Matsushima, director of the central bank's Research and Statistics Department, said that the result of the June tankan corporate survey was in line with the BOJ's assessment of Japan's economic recovery.
Matsushima added that it was difficult to make an overall judgment of the economy based on the tankan alone.
He said a significant improvement in business sentiment among major manufacturers was backed by a rise in exports and also a strong performance in the telecommunications sector.
Although euroyen futures are likely to remain fragile over the short-term, their slide today may well come to a halt shortly on technical factors, one city bank trader said.
A bank trader said: "With today's fall, the March has gotten back to the levels seen three weeks ago, when the possibility of a weak tankan was the dominant view."

The tankan showed that the major manufacturers' diffusion index (DI) -- the percentage difference between corporate managers seeing business conditions favourable and those feeling that conditions are unfavourable -- was plus seven, against plus two in the previous survey in March.
Their September DI forecast was plus eight.
The majority in the market had expected the June DI to fall into negative territory.
Masayuki Matsushima, director of the BOJ's Research and Statistics Department, said the June tankan result was in line with the BOJ's assessment of Japan's economic recovery.
Although euroyen futures are likely to remain fragile over the short term, their slide on Wednesday may well come to a halt soon on technical factors, one city bank trader said.

"The major manufacturers' optimism seen in the tankan was mostly due to a weak yen trend during the period when the survey was conducted. They could easily get pessimistic if the yen appreciates significantly, which is a possiblity too," said a senior money trader.
